findings.title: Migration crashes when embed_category site setting is absent
findings.body: Site settings are only persisted in site_settings when overridden, so most installs have no 'embed_category' row. `execute(...)[0]` is then nil and `nil['id']` raises NoMethodError, aborting the migration (and deployment). The fallback on line 15 has the same problem for 'uncategorized_category_id'. The lookups must handle an empty result set.

findings.title: Migration interpolates stored host values directly into SQL and stores them unnormalized
findings.body: Each legacy host string `h` is interpolated unescaped into the INSERT statement, so a host value containing a single quote breaks the migration and is a SQL-injection vector. Additionally the raw legacy values (which per the old specs may be like 'http://discourse.org' or 'https://example.com/1234') are inserted verbatim, bypassing EmbeddableHost's scheme/path stripping; EmbeddableHost.record_for_host compares lower(host) against the bare URI host, so such migrated rows will never match and embedding for those sites silently breaks after upgrade.

findings.title: before_validation crashes on a nil host instead of failing validation
findings.body: `self.host.sub!(...)` raises NoMethodError when host is nil, e.g. an admin POSTs an embeddable_host with a blank/missing host field from Admin::EmbeddableHostsController. Instead of a 422 validation error via render_json_error, the request 500s. Guard against nil (or use non-mutating sub with to_s) and add a presence validation.

findings.title: update/destroy raise NoMethodError for a nonexistent host id
findings.body: `EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` returns nil for an unknown id, and both update (via save_host calling host.host=) and destroy (line 16, host.destroy) then raise NoMethodError, producing a 500 instead of a 404. This is reachable with a stale admin page after a host was deleted in another tab.

findings.title: edit action crashes when the host has no resolvable category
findings.body: `this.get('host.category.id')` throws if host.category is undefined. That happens for a host whose category was deleted, and also after save() sets `host.category` to Discourse.Category.findById(categoryId) which is undefined when no category was chosen (the server silently substitutes the uncategorized category, which the client does not mirror). Clicking Edit then breaks the admin page; use a safe get (host.category && host.category.id) and sync the category returned by the server.

findings.title: No uniqueness constraint on host allows duplicate hosts with conflicting categories
findings.body: There is no uniqueness validation on host and the migration creates no unique index. Admins can create two rows for the same host pointing at different categories; record_for_host then returns whichever row the database happens to return first, so embedded topics are filed into an unpredictable category and host_allowed?/category selection becomes nondeterministic.

findings.title: Fabricator file contents are swapped between the two fabricator files
findings.body: category_fabricator.rb now defines only Fabricator(:embeddable_host), while the new embeddable_host_fabricator.rb defines :category, :diff_category, :happy_category and :private_category. Fabrication loads every file so tests still pass, but the swapped names are misleading and invite a future duplicate-definition error when someone adds a fabricator to the file matching its name.
